correctness.rationale: The active-normal proof was reconstructed in both combinatorial chambers and at \(c=2\). For \(1<c<2\), each vertex is a signed permutation of \((1,c-1,0)\); for \(2<c<3\), of \((1,1,c-2)\). In each case a unique tetrahedral direction has dot products \(-1\) or \(-3\) against every active outer normal. The universal three-dimensional lower bound gives equality at four. Endpoint arguments correctly show that one direction can illuminate at most one octahedron or cube vertex, yielding six and eight. The package verifier blob 8b977d72798cd50d3a2b24f64faef50cc6162349 independently exhausts all sign/normal patterns and the endpoint constructions.

value.rationale: The family continuously interpolates between two classical extremal polytopes and passes through three named Archimedean solids. Determining both endpoint jumps and the dimension-minimal constant on the entire open interval, with one fixed illuminating tetrahedron, is a natural complete phase classification rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
residual_risks: The argument is highly specific to the exact active-normal patterns of this family.

final_claim: For \(K_c=[-1,1]^3\cap\{x:\lVert x\rVert_1\le c\}\), \(1\le c\le3\), the ordinary illumination number is \(6\) at \(c=1\), \(4\) for every \(1<c<3\), and \(8\) at \(c=3\). The same four tetrahedral directions illuminate the whole open family, including the regular truncated octahedron, cuboctahedron, and regular truncated cube.
limitations: The theorem is three-dimensional and specific to this cube--octahedron intersection family.
It concerns ordinary illumination number, not weighted illumination parameters or arbitrary 1-symmetric bodies.
